name: Alcohol as sleep aid

lead: Some people have a drink to fall asleep faster. Alcohol brings on drowsiness quickly, which is the appeal. The trade-off people in looksmaxxing circles discuss is what happens afterward: disrupted sleep that they say shows up as a puffier, more tired-looking face.

Wikipedia's article on alcohol's effects says it causes drowsiness while disrupting sleep architecture, particularly later REM sleep, lowers sleep quality and can worsen existing sleep problems. Alcohol also reduces vasopressin release, which Wikipedia links to dehydration. The facial puffiness claim comes from forums; the reference source does not discuss puffiness, though it notes the dehydrating effect and the flush reaction.

paras: People use an evening drink or nightcap close to bedtime, and many in appearance communities instead cut it out in the hours before sleep, since they connect it to waking up puffy and tired. Effects on sleep show up the same night.

Disrupted sleep during and after drinking, lower sleep quality and worsening of existing sleep problems. In people who stop after dependence, lingering sleep disruption is described as a strong predictor of relapse (a 2007 study cited by Wikipedia). Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant, and dehydration contributes to hangover severity.

web.title: Effects of alcohol on the body - Wikipedia

angle.text: People drink in the evening to fall asleep faster, and looksmaxxing forums connect the resulting broken sleep with morning puffiness and a tired look. Reference sources document the drowsiness and sleep disruption; the facial effects are a community claim.

lead: Using alcohol as a sleep aid means drinking in the evening to fall asleep faster. Wikipedia reports that alcohol can cause drowsiness while disrupting sleep architecture, particularly later REM sleep, and that it lowers sleep quality and can greatly worsen existing sleep problems [1].

Alcohol also reduces production and release of vasopressin, and dehydration is described as a factor in hangover severity [1]. No published study cited here links alcohol use to facial puffiness; this claim circulates in looksmaxxing communities.

paras: Wikipedia says that after quitting alcohol, sleep typically normalises into deeper, more consistent rest [1]. In alcohol-dependent patients, persistent sleep EEG abnormalities during abstinence were reported by Feige and colleagues in 2007 as a strong predictor of relapse [1].
No studies found on alcohol as a sleep aid for appearance. Wikipedia's article references a 2007 study on sleep EEG in abstinent alcohol-dependent patients [1].
